sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的外面是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，帮助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即在 nytimes.com slash subscribe 订阅即可享受特惠。

sentences.en: Can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 你能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: Fred, can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，你能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: The internet is a little wonky.
sentences.zh: 网络有点不稳定。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, here's Arizona, so you know that she hears it really faSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里是亚利桑那州，所以你知道她听得非常清楚。

sentences.en: I think we're going to call you.
sentences.zh: 我想我们要给你打电话了。

sentences.en: I think we're going to call you back on a, for the first time in a really long time, a landline.
sentences.zh: 我想我们要用一种真的很久没用过的方式给你回电话，用座机。

sentences.en: Hey, Fred, it's Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 嘿，弗雷德，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: You can hear me okay?
sentences.zh: 你能听清我说话吗？

sentences.en: I can hear you.
sentences.zh: 我能听到。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 太完美了。

sentences.en: So, Fred, where exactly am I reaching you?
sentences.zh: 那么，弗雷德，我究竟是在哪里联系到你的？

sentences.en: I'm in Portal, Arizona, in a little community called Arizona Sky Village.
sentences.zh: 我在亚利桑那州的波塔尔，在一个叫亚利桑那天空村的小社区里。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And it's a very rural community.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常乡村化的社区。

sentences.en: So, our internet and phone lines are not very good.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的网络和电话线都不是很好。

sentences.en: And the nearest grocery store is 60 miles away.
sentences.zh: 最近的杂货店在60英里外。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And why would you choose to live in such a remote place with such bad internet?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么会选择住在这样一个网络这么差的偏远地方呢？

sentences.en: Because the sky is dark.
sentences.zh: 因为这里的夜空很黑。

sentences.en: It's like the sky was 100 years ago before cities encrouched on all of the country.
sentences.zh: 就像100年前城市侵占整个乡村之前的天空一样。

sentences.en: I guess you'd call it an astronomy development.
sentences.zh: 我想你会称它为一个天文开发区。

sentences.en: And mainly amateur astronomers who have built homes here far from city lights for the express purpose of studying the sky.
sentences.zh: 这里主要是一些业余天文学家，为了专门研究天空，远离城市灯光，在这里建了房子。

sentences.en: So, it's literally a community where once the sun goes down, it's pitch black, and some, perhaps all of you, are stargazing.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的是一个太阳一下山就漆黑一片的社区，你们中的一些人，甚至可能所有人，都在仰望星空。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Well, I think I'm beginning to understand why you might have the nickname that you do.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我开始明白你为什么会有那个外号了。

sentences.en: Can you just tell our listeners what that nickname is?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们的听众说说那个外号是什么吗？

sentences.en: My nickname is Mr. Eclipse.
sentences.zh: 我的外号是“日食先生”。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today's total solar eclipse will be watched by millions of people across North America.
sentences.zh: 今天的日全食将吸引北美数以百万计的人观看。

sentences.en: None of them as closely as Fred Espinak, a longtime NASA scientist who's devoted his entire life to studying, chasing, and popularizing the wonder that is an eclipse.
sentences.zh: 但没有人像弗雷德·埃斯佩纳克那样关注得那么密切，他是一位长期在NASA工作的科学家，把毕生精力都奉献给了研究、追逐和推广日食这一奇观。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月8日，星期一。

sentences.en: Fred, help me understand how you become Mr. Eclipse.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，帮我理解一下你是怎么成为“日食先生”的。

sentences.en: How you go from being Fred to this seemingly very hard-earned nickname of Mr. Eclipse.
sentences.zh: 你是怎么从弗雷德变成这个听起来来之不易的外号——“日食先生”的？

sentences.en: Well, I was visiting my grandparents at their summer home, and it was a partial eclipse of the sun back in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是20世纪60年代初，我去祖父母的避暑山庄探亲，当时正值日偏食。

sentences.en: And I was a 10 or 12-year-old kid.
sentences.zh: 我那时是个10岁或12岁的孩子。

sentences.en: I got my parents to get me a small telescope, and I watched some of the partial phases, and it was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 我让父母给我买了一个小型望远镜，我观看了一些日偏食的阶段，觉得非常有趣。

sentences.en: And I started reading about eclipses, and I found out that as interesting as a partial eclipse is, a total eclipse is far more interesting.
sentences.zh: 我开始阅读关于日食的书籍，我发现虽然日偏食很有趣，但日全食要有趣得多。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: The moon is only one four-hundredth the diameter of the sun.
sentences.zh: 月球的直径只有太阳的四百分之一。

sentences.en: It's tiny compared to the sun, but it's 400 times closer to the Earth.
sentences.zh: 跟太阳比起来它太小了，但它离地球近了400倍。

sentences.en: So it's just this incredible coincidence that the moon and the sun appear to be the same size in the sky.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个不可思议的巧合，月亮和太阳在天空中的大小看起来是一样的。

sentences.en: And once in a while, the moon passes directly between the Earth and the sun, and you're plunged into this very strange midday twilight.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，月球会直接运行到地球和太阳之间，你就会陷入这种非常奇怪的正午暮色中。

sentences.en: But they're limited to very small geographic areas to see a total eclipse.
sentences.zh: 但能看到日全食的地理区域非常有限。

sentences.en: And this little book I was studying had a map of the world showing upcoming paths of total solar eclipses.
sentences.zh: 我正在研究的那本小书上有一张世界地图，上面显示了即将到来的日全食路径。

sentences.en: And I realized that one was passing through North America about 600 miles from where I lived.
sentences.zh: 我意识到其中一条将穿过北美洲，离我住的地方大约600英里。

sentences.en: And that eclipse was in 1970.
sentences.zh: 那次日食是在1970年。

sentences.en: And I was reading about this in 1963, 1964, and I made a promise to myself that I was going to get to that eclipse in 1970 to see it, because I thought it was a one chance
sentences.zh: 我在1963年、1964年读到了关于它的消息，我向自己保证，我一定要在1970年去看那次日食，因为我认为这是一生

sentences.en: in a lifetime to see a total eclipse of the sun.
sentences.zh: 只有一次的机会去观看日全食。

sentences.en: So just to be very clear, you see a partial eclipse, and you immediately think to yourself, that was fine, but I need the real thing.
sentences.zh: 所以为了搞清楚，你看到了一次日偏食，然后你立刻对自己说，那挺不错，但我需要真正的日食。

sentences.en: I need a full eclipse.
sentences.zh: 我需要一次完整的日食。

sentences.en: And you happen to find out around this time that a real eclipse is coming, but in seven years.
sentences.zh: 你恰好在这个时候发现一次真正的日食即将来临，但要在七年之后。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, there were other eclipses between that time and seven years in the future, but they were in other parts of the world, and I couldn't buy an airplane ticket and fly to
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在那段时间和未来的七年之间还有其他日食，但它们在世界的其他地方，我买不起机票飞往

sentences.en: Europe or Australia.
sentences.zh: 欧洲或澳大利亚。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And by 1970,
I'd been waiting for this, and by this point, I had just gotten a driver's license, and I convinced my parents to let me drive the car 600 miles to get down into
sentences.zh: 我已经等了很久，到这个时候，我刚刚拿到驾照，我游说父母让我开车600英里去

sentences.en: the path of totality to see this great event.
sentences.zh: 全食带去观看这个伟大的盛事。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wait, from where to where?
sentences.zh: 等等，从哪儿到哪儿？

sentences.en: From Staten Island, New York, down to a little town in North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 从纽约斯塔滕岛到底层北卡罗来纳州的一个小镇。

sentences.en: How did you convince your parents to let you do that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么说服父母让你这么做的？

sentences.en: I mean, that's...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那...

sentences.en: Well, I had seven years to work on it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有七年的时间来做思想工作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, you know, I was just a nerdy kid.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我只是个书呆子小孩。

sentences.en: I didn't get into trouble.
sentences.zh: 我不惹麻烦。

sentences.en: I was interested in science.
sentences.zh: 我对科学感兴趣。

sentences.en: I was out in the woods studying frogs and wildlife and stuff, so this was just a natural progression of the type of things I would normally do.
sentences.zh: 我在树林里研究青蛙和野生动物之类的东西，所以这只是我平时会做的事情的自然延续。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, I wonder if you can describe this journey you end up taking from Staten Island.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想知道你是否能描述一下你从斯塔滕岛出发的这段旅程。

sentences.en: How does the trip unfold as you're headed on this 600 mile?
sentences.zh: 当你踏上这600英里的旅程时，整个行程是如何展开的？

sentences.en: So, I think on March 6th, 1970, it was a Friday.
sentences.zh: 我想在1970年3月6日，那天是星期五。

sentences.en: My friend and I left to drive to the eclipse path.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友出发开车去日食路径。

sentences.en: We probably got on the road probably at 5 a.m.
sentences.zh: 我们可能早上5点就上路了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Because it was going to be a very long day.
sentences.zh: 因为这将是非常漫长的一天。

sentences.en: And we've got a detailed map in the car, which I've plotted the eclipse path on.
sentences.zh: 我们在车里有一张详细的地图，我在上面标出了日食路径。

sentences.en: And we're just trying to get far enough south to get into the path of the eclipse, which for us is easternmost Virginia or eastern North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想向南开得足够远，进入日食路径，对我们来说就是弗吉尼亚州最东部或北卡罗来纳州东部。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I drive and drive and drive all day long, a very long day.
sentences.zh: 我开车，开车，开了一整天，非常漫长的一天。

sentences.en: We get down to North Carolina right about maybe 6 p.m., and we just see this little town in North Carolina that we're driving through.
sentences.zh: 我们在傍晚6点左右到达北卡罗来纳州，我们看到北卡罗来纳州有一个我们正开车穿过的小镇。

sentences.en: And it happens to have a convenient motel right in the center of the path.
sentences.zh: 而且它刚好在路径中心有一个很方便的汽车旅馆。

sentences.en: And that was good enough.
sentences.zh: 这就足够了。

sentences.en: Got a room available.
sentences.zh: 有空房。

sentences.en: And we check in, and that's where we're going to watch the eclipse from.
sentences.zh: 我们登记入住，这就是我们打算观看日食的地方。

sentences.en: And the next morning was eclipse day.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上就是日食日。

sentences.en: It was a bright, crisp, sunny morning.
sentences.zh: 那是一个明亮、干爽、晴朗的早晨。

sentences.en: There weren't any clouds at all in the sky.
sentences.zh: 天空中一点云也没有。

sentences.en: And I was amazed that outside the back of the motel in this grassy field, there were dozens and dozens of people with telescopes out there,
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶地发现，在汽车旅馆后面的这片草地上，有几十甚至上百人架着望远镜在那儿，

sentences.en: specifically there for the eclipse that morning.
sentences.zh: 他们就是专程为了那天早上的日食而来的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: We were really excited about this.
sentences.zh: 我们对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: We set up my telescope, and we had another camera set up to watch it.
sentences.zh: 我们架好了我的望远镜，还架设了另一台相机来拍摄。

sentences.en: And we walked around and marveled at some of the other people and their telescopes and discussed the eclipse with them.
sentences.zh: 我们四处走动，惊叹于其他人的望远镜，并与他们讨论日食。

sentences.en: And the eclipse started probably around noon or 1 in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 日食大概在中午或下午1点左右开始。

sentences.en: Describe the actual event itself, the eclipse.
sentences.zh: 描述一下活动本身，也就是日食。

sentences.en: How did it begin?
sentences.zh: 它是怎么开始的？

sentences.en: Well, all solar eclipses begin as a partial eclipse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所有的日食都是从日偏食开始的。

sentences.en: And the sun is gradually covered by the moon as the moon takes larger and larger pieces out of the sun as it slowly crawls across the sun's surface.
sentences.zh: 当月亮在太阳表面缓慢爬行时，它从太阳上咬下越来越大的缺口，太阳也逐渐被月亮遮住。

sentences.en: And you don't really notice much going on with the naked eye.
sentences.zh: 用肉眼你其实注意不到太多变化。

sentences.en: It's really only in the last 10 minutes or so that you start to notice changes in the environment.
sentences.zh: 真的只有在最后大约10分钟里，你才会开始注意到环境的变化。

sentences.en: Because now enough of the sun has been covered, upwards of maybe 90% of the sun.
sentences.zh: 因为现在足够多的太阳被遮住了，达到了太阳的90%以上。

sentences.en: And you start to notice the temperature falling.
sentences.zh: 你开始注意到气温下降。

sentences.en: There's a chill in the air.
sentences.zh: 空气中有一种寒意。

sentences.en: Also, since so much of the sun is covered, the daylight starts to take on kind of an anemic quality.
sentences.zh: 此外，由于如此多的太阳被遮住，日光开始呈现一种贫血般的特质。

sentences.en: It's weak.
sentences.zh: 它很微弱。

sentences.en: The sun is still too bright to look at, but the surroundings, the environment is not as bright as it was a half hour earlier.
sentences.zh: 太阳依然太亮而无法直视，但周围环境已经不如半小时前那么明亮了。

sentences.en: You start to notice animals reacting to the dwindling sunlight.
sentences.zh: 你开始注意到动物对逐渐消失的阳光做出反应。

sentences.en: They start acting like it's sunset and they start performing some of their evening rituals, like birds roosting, perhaps calling their evening songs.
sentences.zh: 它们开始表现得像是日落一样，并开始进行它们的一些晚间仪式，比如鸟儿回巢，也许开始鸣唱它们的晚间歌曲。

sentences.en: And plants start closing up in the dropping sunlight and in the dropping temperatures.
sentences.zh: 随着阳光和温度的下降，植物开始闭合。

sentences.en: And there's an acceleration now of all these effects.
sentences.zh: 现在所有这些效应都在加速。

sentences.en: The temperature drop, the drop in the sunlight, it starts happening faster and faster and getting darker and darker.
sentences.zh: 气温下降，阳光减少，这一切开始发生得越来越快，天色也越来越黑。

sentences.en: And maybe about a minute before the total eclipse began, we noticed strange patterns on the ground beneath us, on the grassy field that we were on.
sentences.zh: 大约在日全食开始前一分钟，我们注意到脚下的地面上、我们所在的草地上出现了奇怪的图案。

sentences.en: These ripples racing across the field.
sentences.zh: 这些涟漪在草地上飞驰而过。

sentences.en: And these are something called shadow bands.
sentences.zh: 这些东西被称为“日影带”。

sentences.en: They look a lot like the rippling patterns that you would see on the bottom of a swimming pool.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来非常像你在游泳池底部看到的涟漪图案。

sentences.en: Bands of light and dark and moving very quickly across the ground.
sentences.zh: 明暗相间的带子在地面上快速移动。

sentences.en: The sky is, it's a dark blue and it's getting darker rapidly in this dwindling sunlight.
sentences.zh: 天空呈深蓝色，在这渐弱的阳光下迅速变暗。

sentences.en: And you go from daylight to twilight in just 10 or 20 seconds.
sentences.zh: 你只需10到20秒就能从白昼变成黄昏。

sentences.en: It's almost like someone has the hand on the rheostat, turns the house lights down in the theater.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像有人把手放在变阻器上，把剧院里的室内灯光调暗了一样。

sentences.en: You just see the light just go right down.
sentences.zh: 你只看到光线直直地暗下去。

sentences.en: And the sky gets dark enough that the corona, the outer atmosphere of the sun, starts emerging from the background sky.
sentences.zh: 天空变得足够黑，以至于日冕，即太阳的外层大气，开始从背景天空中显现出来。

sentences.en: This ring or halo of gas that surrounds the sun.
sentences.zh: 这个围绕着太阳的气体环或光晕。

sentences.en: And it's visible around the moon, which is in silhouette against the sun.
sentences.zh: 它在以太阳为剪影的月亮周围清晰可见。

sentences.en: And along one edge of the moon is this bright bead of sunlight, because that's the last remaining piece of the sun before it becomes total.
sentences.zh: 沿着月亮的一个边缘是这颗明亮的阳光珠，因为这是太阳在变成日全食前最后剩下的部分。

sentences.en: And this is the diamond ring effect, because you've got the ring of the corona and this dazzling jewel along one edge of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是钻石环效应，因为你拥有日冕的光环以及沿着它一个边缘的这颗耀眼的宝石。

sentences.en: You only get to see this for 10 or 15 seconds.
sentences.zh: 你只能看到这个景象10到15秒。

sentences.en: It's very fleeting before the moon completely covers the sun's disk.
sentences.zh: 在月亮完全遮住太阳圆盘之前，它是非常短暂的。

sentences.en: And totality begins.
sentences.zh: 然后日全食开始了。

sentences.en: Suddenly you're in this twilight of the moon's shadow.
sentences.zh: 突然间，你身处月球阴影的这个暮色之中。

sentences.en: And you look around the horizon, and you're seeing the colors of sunrise or sunset
sentences.zh: 你环顾地平线，你会看到日出或日落的颜色

sentences.en: 360 degrees around the horizon, because you're looking out the edge of the moon's shadow.
sentences.zh: 围绕着地平线360度铺开，因为你正望着月亮阴影的边缘。

sentences.en: And looking back up into the sky, the sun is gone now.
sentences.zh: 再次抬头望向天空，太阳已经消失了。

sentences.en: And you see this black disk of the moon in silhouette, surrounded by the sun's corona.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到月亮黑色的剪影盘旋其中，被太阳的日冕所环绕。

sentences.en: Maybe this says more about my nature than anything else, but what you're describing a little bit feels like the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 也许这更能说明我的天性，但你所描述的这种感觉，多少有点像是世界末日。

sentences.en: Well, I think when you see this all transpire, you can easily understand how people thought this was the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想当你亲眼目睹这一切发生时，你很容易理解为什么人们会认为这是世界末日。

sentences.en: Because it seems far outside of the realms of nature.
sentences.zh: 因为这似乎远远超出了大自然的范畴。

sentences.en: It seems supernatural.
sentences.zh: 它看起来像是超自然的。

sentences.en: So you can see how people panicked that didn't understand what was going on.
sentences.zh: 所以你能明白那些不了解状况的人为什么会惊慌失措。

sentences.en: That was not your reaction?
sentences.zh: 你的反应不是这样的吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是的。

sentences.en: I think it's a sense of belonging, belonging to this incredible universe.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种归属感，对这个不可思议的宇宙的归属感。

sentences.en: Both belonging and a humbleness that how minuscule we are, and yet we're a part of this fantastic cosmic wheel of motion in the solar system.
sentences.zh: 既有归属感，又有一种谦卑感：我们是多么微不足道，然而我们又是太阳系中这场奇妙的宇宙运动齿轮的一部分。

sentences.en: You almost get a three-dimensional sense of the motions of the earth and the moon around the sun when you see this sort of clockwork displayed right in front of you,
sentences.zh: 当你看到这种类似钟表发条的机制就在你面前展现时，

sentences.en: this mechanics of the eclipse taking place.
sentences.zh: 也就是日食发生的这种力学原理，

sentences.en: It's almost like lifts you up off the planet and you can look back down at the solar system and see how it's all put together.
sentences.zh: 你几乎会有一种被带离地球的感觉，能够回过头来俯瞰整个太阳系，看它是如何组合在一起的。

sentences.en: And you've only got to, in that case, in that particular eclipse, it was only two and a half minutes to look at this.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，在那场特定的日食中，你只有两分半钟的时间来观察。

sentences.en: Well, there's kind of a clock in your head saying you don't have much of this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你脑海里仿佛有个时钟在提醒你，你的时间不多了。

sentences.en: You don't have much of it.
sentences.zh: 你的时间真的不多了。

sentences.en: It almost seems like time stops, and at the same time, all of a sudden, the eclipse is over.
sentences.zh: 时间仿佛静止了，但与此同时，转瞬间，日食就结束了。

sentences.en: Those two minutes just raced by.
sentences.zh: 那两分钟就这样转瞬即逝。

sentences.en: And it's over, and all of a sudden, the diamond ring forms again on the opposite side of the moon as the sun starts to become uncovered at the end of totality.
sentences.zh: 它结束了，随着全食阶段接近尾声，太阳开始显露，钻石环突然又在月亮的另一侧形成了。

sentences.en: And the diamond ring appears.
sentences.zh: 然后钻石环出现了。

sentences.en: It grows incredibly bright in just a few seconds, and you can't look at it anymore.
sentences.zh: 它在短短几秒钟内变得无比明亮，你再也无法直视它了。

sentences.en: It's too bright.
sentences.zh: 它太耀眼了。

sentences.en: You've got to put your filters back on and cover your telescope with a solar filter so it doesn't get damaged.
sentences.zh: 你必须重新戴上滤光镜，用太阳滤镜盖住你的望远镜，以免它受损。

sentences.en: And you're trembling because of this event.
sentences.zh: 而你正因为这一壮观的景象而浑身颤抖。

sentences.en: Everybody was cheering and shouting and yelling.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在欢呼、呐喊、尖叫。

sentences.en: I mean, you would have thought you were at a sports game and the home team just scored a touchdown.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可能会以为自己身处体育赛场，而主队刚刚完成了一次达阵。

sentences.en: Just everybody screaming at the top of their lungs.
sentences.zh: 所有人都在竭尽全力地尖叫。

sentences.en: And I immediately started thinking that this can't be a once-in-a-lifetime experience.
sentences.zh: 我立刻开始想，这绝不能是一生仅有一次的体验。

sentences.en: I've got to see this again.
sentences.zh: 我一定要再看一次。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜洛。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天都制作“拼字蜜蜂”和“字母包厢”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特性。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始游玩。

sentences.en: Okay, so Fred, it's the early 1970s, and you are not Mr. Eclipse yet.
sentences.zh: 好的，弗雷德，那是20世纪70年代初，你还不是“日食先生”。

sentences.en: You're just a kid who felt something very big when you watched an eclipse.
sentences.zh: 你只是一个在观看日食时感受到极震撼冲击的孩子。

sentences.en: So how did you end up becoming the premier authority that you now are on eclipses?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何成为如今首屈一指的日食权威的呢？

sentences.en: Well, after that 1970 eclipse, I started looking into upcoming solar eclipses so I could get a chance to see the sun's corona again.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在1970年那场日食之后，我开始查阅即将发生日食的信息，以便有机会再次看到太阳的日冕。

sentences.en: And the next total eclipse was in eastern Canada in July of 1972.
sentences.zh: 下一次日全食是在1972年7月的加拿大东部。

sentences.en: And I started thinking about that eclipse, and by then I was going to be in college.
sentences.zh: 我开始考虑那场日食，到那时我就要上大学了。

sentences.en: And I started planning, because that one was still something I could drive to.
sentences.zh: 我开始做计划，因为那场日食我依然可以开车前往。

sentences.en: It was 1,200 miles instead of 600 miles.
sentences.zh: 距离是1200英里，而不是600英里。

sentences.en: So the summer of 1972 rolls around, and I drove up to the eclipse in Quebec to see totality and was unfortunately clouded out of the eclipse.
sentences.zh: 于是，1972年夏天到了，我开车去魁北克观看日食的全食阶段，但不幸的是，由于多云，我没能看成日食。

sentences.en: I saw some of the partial phases, but clouds moved in and obscured the sun for that view of the sun's corona.
sentences.zh: 我看到了一些偏食阶段，但云层飘了过来，挡住了太阳，遮蔽了我观看日冕的视线。

sentences.en: You were robbed.
sentences.zh: 你被剥夺了机会。

sentences.en: I was robbed.
sentences.zh: 我确实被剥夺了。

sentences.en: And I realized, well, I've got to expand my outlook on what's an acceptable distance to travel to see a total eclipse.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，好吧，我必须开阔眼界，重新定义去看日全食的可接受旅行距离。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Because the next total eclipse then, in 1973, was through the Sahara Desert in northern Africa.
sentences.zh: 因为接下来在1973年的日全食，穿过了北非的撒哈拉沙漠。

sentences.en: So I traveled to the Sahara Desert for the eclipse, where we had decent weather.
sentences.zh: 所以我为了日食去了撒哈拉沙漠，那里的天气还算不错。

sentences.en: Not perfect, but decent weather that we got to see totality there.
sentences.zh: 虽然不完美，但天气还算可以，我们在那里看到了全食。

sentences.en: You saw totality in the desert?
sentences.zh: 你在沙漠里看到了日全食？

sentences.en: In the desert, in the Sahara Desert.
sentences.zh: 在沙漠里，在撒哈拉沙漠里。

sentences.en: And after that, it was just trying to get to every total eclipse I possibly could get to.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我所做的就是设法赶上我能去的所有日全食。

sentences.en: At this point, you're clearly starting to become an eclipse chaser.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，你显然已经开始成为一名日食追逐者了。

sentences.en: And I don't even know if such a thing existed at that moment.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道在那时是否存在这种说法。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't think, I don't know if it was called that then, but certainly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想，我不知道当时是不是这么叫的，但确实如此。

sentences.en: And if you'll permit me a question that might seem maybe dopey to someone in your field,
sentences.zh: 如果你允许我问一个在你们行家看来可能有点蠢的问题，

sentences.en: after you've seen one or two or three of these, do they start to kind of blend in together and become a little bit the same?
sentences.zh: 在你看了其中的一两次或三次之后，它们会不会开始融为一体，变得有点千篇一律？

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不会。

sentences.en: Each one is distinctly different.
sentences.zh: 每一次都截然不同。

sentences.en: The sun itself is dramatically different.
sentences.zh: 太阳本身就有着巨大的差异。

sentences.en: The sun's corona is different at each eclipse because the corona is a product of the sun's magnetic field.
sentences.zh: 每一次日食时太阳的日冕都不同，因为日冕是太阳磁场的产物。

sentences.en: And that magnetic field is changing every day.
sentences.zh: 而这个磁场每天都在变化。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So the details, the fine structure in the sun's corona is always different.
sentences.zh: 所以太阳日冕的细节和精细结构总是各不相同。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So every eclipse is dramatically different, the appearance of the sun's corona.
sentences.zh: 因此，每一次日食都是大不相同的，太阳日冕的外观也各异。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: If you look at one Renoir, it's not the same as the next one.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一幅雷诺阿的作品，它和下一幅是不一样的。

sentences.en: And you're describing the corona of each eclipse as its own work of art, basically.
sentences.zh: 你基本上把每一次日食的日冕都描述为它自己的艺术品。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So as you're chasing these eclipses around the world, what is the place of an eclipse in your day-to-day academic studies and, soon enough, your professional work?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你在世界各地追逐这些日食时，日食在你日常的学术研究中，以及不久后的职业生涯中处于什么地位？

sentences.en: So I went to grad school at the University of Toledo and did some work at the Kitt Peak National Observatory,
sentences.zh: 我在托莱多大学读研究生，并在基特峰国家天文台做了一些工作，

sentences.en: learning the ins and outs of photometric photometry, that is, measuring the brightness of stars.
sentences.zh: 学习光度测量的方方面面，也就是测量恒星的亮度。

sentences.en: And eventually, this led to a job opening at the NASA Goddard Space Flight Center.
sentences.zh: 最终，这为我在美国国家航空航天局戈达德太空飞行中心争取到一个工作职位创造了机会。

sentences.en: And I got interested in the idea of predicting eclipses and started studying the mathematics of how to do this.
sentences.zh: 我对预测日食的想法产生了兴趣，并开始研究如何做到这一点的数学原理。

sentences.en: And I sort of took it over unofficially and started publishing these technical maps and details.
sentences.zh: 我有点非官方地接手了这项工作，并开始发布这些技术地图和详细信息。

sentences.en: And we published about a dozen books through NASA on upcoming eclipses.
sentences.zh: 我们通过NASA出版了大约十多本关于即将发生日食的书籍。

sentences.en: People would just write me a letter and say they wanted a copy of the eclipse bulletin for such and such an eclipse.
sentences.zh: 人们会给我写信，说他们想要某某日食的日食简报复印件。

sentences.en: And I would stuff it in an envelope and mail it to them.
sentences.zh: 然后我就会把它塞进信封里寄给他们。

sentences.en: So you take it upon yourself to make sure that everyone is going to know when the next eclipse is coming.
sentences.zh: 所以你承担起了责任，确保每个人都能知道下一次日食何时到来。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And no doubt during this period, you keep going to each and every eclipse.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，在此期间，你一直在参加每一次日食。

sentences.en: And I wonder which of them stand out to you.
sentences.zh: 我在想其中有哪些对你来说最深刻。

sentences.en: Well, I've seen total eclipses from Australia, from Africa, from the Altiplanos in Bolivia,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我已经在澳大利亚、非洲、玻利维亚的高原看过日全食，

sentences.en: from the ice sheet on the coast of Antarctica, and even from northern China on the edge of the Gobi Desert.
sentences.zh: 在南极洲海岸的冰盖上看过，甚至在戈壁沙漠边缘的中国北方也看过。

sentences.en: But one of the most notable eclipses for me was I traveled to India to see a 41-second eclipse, which was very short.
sentences.zh: 但对我而言最引人注目的日食之一，是我前往印度去观看一场持续41秒、非常短暂的日食。

sentences.en: And besides seeing a great eclipse in India, I also met my future wife there.
sentences.zh: 除了在印度看到了一场精彩的日食，我还在那里遇到了我未来的妻子。

sentences.en: She was on the same trip.
sentences.zh: 她和我在同一个旅行团里。

sentences.en: I have to hear that story.
sentences.zh: 我一定要听听这个故事。

sentences.en: Well, she had been trying to see a total eclipse for about 25 years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她大约25年来一直试图观看日全食。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: She tried to see the 1970 eclipse, but her friends who were going to drive down from Pennsylvania down to North Carolina sort of talked her out of it at the 11th hour.
sentences.zh: 她曾试图观看1970年的日食，但原本打算从宾夕法尼亚州开车南下到北卡罗来纳州的朋友在最后一刻劝阻了她。

sentences.en: They talked her out of seeing the same eclipse that was your first total eclipse that was so important to you.
sentences.zh: 他们劝她放弃了那场对你如此重要、也是你的第一场日全食的观测。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they talked her out of it because from Pennsylvania, they were going to have maybe a 90% eclipse.
sentences.zh: 他们劝她放弃是因为从宾夕法尼亚州出发，他们大概只能看到90%的日偏食。

sentences.en: They didn't know any better.
sentences.zh: 他们当时并不懂这些。

sentences.en: They thought that was good enough.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得那样就足够好了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And she regretted that decision.
sentences.zh: 而她对那个决定感到后悔。

sentences.en: So then she said, OK, well, I got to get to the next total eclipse, which was in Quebec in 1972, the same one that was my second eclipse.
sentences.zh: 所以她说，好吧，我必须去看下一次日全食，也就是1972年在魁北克的那场，那也是我的第二场日食。

sentences.en: And we were probably within five miles of each other in Quebec.
sentences.zh: 我们在魁北克时，彼此的距离可能只有五英里远。

sentences.en: And we were both clouded out.
sentences.zh: 结果我们俩都因为多云而错过了。

sentences.en: Then she was married.
sentences.zh: 后来她结婚了。

sentences.en: She was raising kids.
sentences.zh: 她抚养着孩子。

sentences.en: She got busy with domestic life for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 她为家庭生活忙碌了20年。

sentences.en: She became a widow.
sentences.zh: 她后来守寡了。

sentences.en: So now, 1995, there's this 41-second eclipse in India that is very difficult to get to.
sentences.zh: 现在是1995年，印度有一场41秒的日食，很难抵达。

sentences.en: It's halfway around the world.
sentences.zh: 它在地球的另一端。

sentences.en: But she's still itching to see a total eclipse.
sentences.zh: 但她依然渴望去看一次日全食。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And we joined the same expedition, a travel group of 30 eclipse chasers and end up in India for the eclipse.
sentences.zh: 我们参加了同一个探险团，这是一个由30名日食追逐者组成的旅行团，最终为了日食来到了印度。

sentences.en: And we have fantastic weather.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了梦幻般的天气。

sentences.en: It's perfect.
sentences.zh: 完美无瑕。

sentences.en: She was in tears after totality.
sentences.zh: 全食结束后，她激动得泪流满面。

sentences.en: She had been waiting so long to see it.
sentences.zh: 她等这一天已经等了太久了。

sentences.en: And we struck up a friendship on that trip.
sentences.zh: 我们在那次旅行中建立起了友谊。

sentences.en: By the time the 1998 eclipse was taking place in the Caribbean, at that point, we were together.
sentences.zh: 到了1998年加勒比海日食发生时，那时我们已经在一起了。

sentences.en: We went to—that was our first eclipse to observe as a couple.
sentences.zh: 我们去了——那是我们作为情侣观赏的第一场日食。

sentences.en: Mm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I think our wedding cake had a big eclipse on the top of the cake.
sentences.zh: 我想我们的婚礼蛋糕顶部就有一个大大的日食模型。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 完美。

sentences.en: We made a music CD for the wedding that we played during the reception.
sentences.zh: 我们为婚礼制作了一张音乐光盘，在招待会上播放。

sentences.en: And, of course, all the music on the CD had sun and moon themes to it.
sentences.zh: 当然，光盘里的所有音乐都带有太阳和月亮的主题。

sentences.en: In the dark.
sentences.zh: 在黑暗中。

sentences.en: Nothing I can say.
sentences.zh: 我无话可说。

sentences.en: A total eclipse of the heart.
sentences.zh: 心之全蚀。

sentences.en: Of course, a total eclipse of the heart was a must-have.
sentences.zh: 当然，《心之全蚀》是必不可少的。

sentences.en: Had to.
sentences.zh: 必须要有。

sentences.en: Had to.
sentences.zh: 绝对得有。

sentences.en: It strikes me, Fred, that eclipses are such an organizing principle in your life.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，我发现日食是你生活中的一个核心组织原则。

sentences.en: Your life seems to literally orbit around them.
sentences.zh: 你的生活似乎真的是围绕着它们在运行。

sentences.en: When you were a kid, you started planning for them years in advance.
sentences.zh: 你还是个孩子的时候，就开始提前好几年为它们做计划。

sentences.en: This work becomes central to your career.
sentences.zh: 这项工作成为了你职业生涯的核心。

sentences.en: It's how you meet your wife.
sentences.zh: 这也是你结识妻子的方式。

sentences.en: And you said when I asked you about each eclipse that they're all different.
sentences.zh: 当我问你关于每一次日食时，你说它们各不相同。

sentences.en: And, obviously, you're different at each eclipse because time has passed.
sentences.zh: 显然，每一次看日食时的你也不一样，因为时间流逝了。

sentences.en: Your life has changed.
sentences.zh: 你的生活发生了变化。

sentences.en: And it just feels like your life is being lived in a kind of ongoing conversation with this phenomenon of the sun and the moon overlapping.
sentences.zh: 感觉你的生活就像是在与太阳和月亮交迭这一自然现象进行一场持续的对话。

sentences.en: Well, the eclipses are like benchmarks that I can use to figure out what else was going on in my life during these times.
sentences.zh: 嗯，日食就像是路标，我可以借此弄清楚在我生活的这些时期还发生了什么。

sentences.en: Because I remember the dates of every single eclipse I've been to.
sentences.zh: 因为我记得我去过的每一场日食的日期。

sentences.en: And if I see a photograph of the solar corona shot during any particular eclipse, I know what eclipse that was.
sentences.zh: 如果我看到任何一次特定日食期间拍摄的日冕照片，我就能认出那是哪次日食。

sentences.en: I can recognize the pattern of the corona like a fingerprint.
sentences.zh: 我能像认指纹一样认出日冕的图案。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: And I know the year of the eclipse,
sentences.zh: 而且我知道那次日食是哪一年，

sentences.en: it reminds me of when Pat and I got married and between which eclipse we were getting married and had to plan our wedding so it didn't interfere with any kind of eclipse trips.
sentences.zh: 它让我想起帕特和我结婚的时候，以及我们的婚礼夹在两次日食之间，我们不得不精心筹划婚礼，以免与任何日食观测之旅冲突。

sentences.en: And they just serve as sort of benchmarks or markers for the rest of my life of when various eclipses take place.
sentences.zh: 它们就像我余生中各种日食发生时的基准或路标。

sentences.en: So they're easy for marking the passage of time.
sentences.zh: 所以它们很容易用来标记时间的流逝。

sentences.en: So we are, of course, talking to you a few days before this year's eclipse, which I cannot fathom you missing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们当然是在今年的日食前几天采访你，我简直无法想象你会错过它。

sentences.en: So where are you planning to watch this total eclipse?
sentences.zh: 那么你打算去哪里观看这次日全食呢？

sentences.en: Pat and I are leaving for Mazatlan, Mexico, actually tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我和帕特其实明天就要出发去墨西哥马萨特兰了。

sentences.en: And we've got about 80 people joining us down in Mazatlan for this eclipse in our tour group.
sentences.zh: 我们团队大约有80人会去马萨特兰和我们一起看这次日食。

sentences.en: And for you, of course, this year's eclipse is just the latest in a very long line of eclipses.
sentences.zh: 对你来说，今年的日食当然只是你漫长追日生涯中的又一次。

sentences.en: But I think for the rest of us, and here I'm thinking about myself, this is really going to be my first total eclipse, at least that I can remember.
sentences.zh: 但我想对我们其他人来说——这里我指的是我自己——这真的是我的第一次日食，至少是我有记忆以来的第一次。

sentences.en: And for my two little kids, it's absolutely going to be their firSt.
sentences.zh: 对我的两个小孩来说，这绝对是他们的第一次。

sentences.en: And given the hard-earned wisdom that you've accumulated in all your decades of chasing eclipses around the world,
sentences.zh: 鉴于你在世界各地追逐日食的几十年里积累的苦心孤诣的智慧，

sentences.en: I wonder if you can give us just a little bit of advice for how to best live inside this very brief window of a total solar eclipse to make sure, not to be cliched,
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否给我们一点小小的建议，告诉我们如何最好地去经历这短暂的日全食瞬间，确保——免得显得老套——

sentences.en: but that we make it count.
sentences.zh: 但我们要让它不虚此行。

sentences.en: Well, I think one mistake that people tend to make is getting preoccupied with recording everything in their lives, what they had for lunch, what they had for dinner.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为人们容易犯的一个错误是全神贯注于记录生活中的一切，午饭吃了什么，晚饭吃了什么。

sentences.en: And seeing the eclipse is something that you want to witness firsthand.
sentences.zh: 而观看日食是一件你想亲身体验的事情。

sentences.en: Try to be present in seeing the eclipse in the moment of it.
sentences.zh: 尽量活在当下，去亲眼看日食发生的那个瞬间。

sentences.en: So don't get preoccupied with recording every instant of it.
sentences.zh: 所以不要全神贯注于记录它的每一个瞬间。

sentences.en: Sit back and try to take in the entire experience.
sentences.zh: 坐下来，试着去感受整个体验。

sentences.en: Because those several minutes pass by so rapidly, but you'll replay them in your mind over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 因为这短短的几分钟过得太快了，但你会在脑海中一遍又一遍地回味它们。

sentences.en: And you don't want technology getting between you and that experience.
sentences.zh: 你可不想让科技横亘在你和那种体验之间。

sentences.en: And remember to take your eclipse glasses off when totality begins.
sentences.zh: 记住，当全食开始时，要摘下日食眼镜。

sentences.en: Note how dark it gets during totality.
sentences.zh: 注意全食时天色变得有多暗。

sentences.en: Take the glasses off because?
sentences.zh: 摘下眼镜是因为什么？

sentences.en: Well, the glasses protect your eyes from the sun's bright disk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，眼镜可以保护你的眼睛免受太阳明亮盘面的伤害。

sentences.en: But when totality begins, the sun's bright disk is gone.
sentences.zh: 但当全食开始时，太阳明亮的盘面就消失了。

sentences.en: So if you use your solar eclipse glasses to try to look at the corona, you won't see anything.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你用日食眼镜去试图看日冕，你什么也看不见。

sentences.en: You'll just see blackness.
sentences.zh: 你只会看到一片漆黑。

sentences.en: You've got to remove the eclipse glasses in order to see the corona.
sentences.zh: 你必须摘掉日食眼镜才能看到日冕。

sentences.en: And it's completely safe.
sentences.zh: 而且这是绝对安全的。

sentences.en: And it's an incredible sight to behold.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人难以置信的奇观。

sentences.en: But during totality, you just want to look around without the glasses on and take in the sights, take in the horizon, 360 degrees,
sentences.zh: 但在全食期间，你不戴眼镜环顾四周，去欣赏风景、360度的地平线，

sentences.en: surrounding you with these twilight colors and sunset colors.
sentences.zh: 周围环绕着这些暮色和日落的色彩。

sentences.en: You'll easily be able to see Jupiter and Venus shining on either side of the sun during totality.
sentences.zh: 在全食期间，你很容易就能看到木星和金星在太阳两侧闪耀。

sentences.en: And look at the details in the sun's corona.
sentences.zh: 去看看日冕中的细节。

sentences.en: Fine, wispy textures and any possible red prominences hugging against the moon's disk during totality.
sentences.zh: 细腻、飘逸的纹理，以及在全食期间紧贴着月面边缘的任何可能存在的红色日珥。

sentences.en: And let's say it's now the moment of totality.
sentences.zh: 假设现在就是全食的时刻。

sentences.en: And you, Mr. Eclipse, can whisper one thing into someone's ear as they're watching.
sentences.zh: 而你，日食先生，可以在某人观看时在他们耳边呢喃一句话。

sentences.en: What would you say to them?
sentences.zh: 你会对他们说什么？

sentences.en: Enjoy.
sentences.zh: 享受吧。

sentences.en: Just take it all in.
sentences.zh: 尽情去感受这一切。

sentences.en: Well, Fred, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，弗雷德，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: No, thank you.
sentences.zh: 不，谢谢你们。

sentences.en: I hope everybody has some clear sky.
sentences.zh: 我希望每个人都能看到晴朗的天空。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: After today, the next total solar eclipse to be visible from the continental United States will occur 20 years from now, in 2044.
sentences.zh: 过了今天，美国本土能看到的下一次日全食将是20年后的2044年。

sentences.en: In other words, you might as well watch today's.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，今天的日食你最好还是看一看。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: Israel has fired two officers in connection with the deadly airstrike on aid workers from the world's central kitchen,
sentences.zh: 以色列因世界中央厨房援助人员遭致命空袭一事解雇了两名军官，

sentences.en: who were killed last week while delivering food to civilians in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 这些援助人员上周在加沙向平民分发食物时遇害。

sentences.en: In a report released on Friday, Israel blamed their deaths on a string of errors made by the military.
sentences.zh: 以色列周五发布的报告将他们的死归咎于军方的一系列错误。

sentences.en: The airstrike, Israel said, was based on insufficient and incorrect evidence that a passenger traveling with the workers was armed.
sentences.zh: 以色列称，空袭是基于不足且不正确的证据，即与援助人员同行的乘客携带了武器。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Israel said it withdrew a division of ground troops from southern Gaza on Sunday, leaving no soldiers actively patrolling the area.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，以色列称周日从加沙南部撤出一个师的地面部队，没有留下士兵在该地区进行积极巡逻。

sentences.en: The move raises questions about Israel's strategy as the war drags into its sixth month.
sentences.zh: 随着战争进入第六个月，此举引发了对以色列战略的质疑。

sentences.en: In particular, it casts doubt on Israel's plans to invade Rafah, Gaza's southernmost city,
sentences.zh: 特别是，这给以色列入侵加沙最南端城市拉法的计划蒙上了阴影，

sentences.en: an invasion that the United States has asked Israel not to carry out for fear of large-scale civilian casualties.
sentences.zh: 美国曾要求以色列不要进行这场入侵，因为担心造成大规模平民伤亡。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Sidney Harper and Alex Stern, with help from Will Reed and Jessica Chung.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由西德尼·哈珀和亚历克斯·斯特恩制作，威尔·里德和杰西卡·钟提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor, fact-checked by Susan Lee, contains original music by Dan Powell,
sentences.zh: 节目由德文·泰勒剪辑，苏珊·李核实事实，原创音乐由丹·鲍威尔、

sentences.en: Marion Lozato, Alicia Baitube, and Corey Schreppel, and sound design by Alicia Baitube and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 马里恩·洛扎托、艾丽西亚·拜蒂布和科里·施雷佩尔创作，声音设计由艾丽西亚·拜蒂布和丹·鲍威尔完成。

sentences.en: It was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 音响工程由克里斯·伍德负责。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Anthony Wallace.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢安东尼·华莱士。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Memorial.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·米莫尔。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党陷入了一场激烈、混乱有时甚至令人兴奋的权力斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》中，我和萨拉·科尼格将带你了解那些试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何地方收听。
